questions.question: Which female pop superstar holds the all-time record for the most Grammy Awards ever won?
questions.explanation: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy Awards ever won by any artist. She surpassed Georg Solti's long-standing record, cementing her legacy as one of the greatest recording artists of all time. Her wins span multiple categories, including pop, R&B, and country.

questions.question: Which South Korean girl group, known for hits like "DDU-DU DDU-DU," debuted as an idol group in 2016?
questions.explanation: BLACKPINK debuted on August 8, 2016, under YG Entertainment, making them one of the fastest K-pop groups to achieve global fame. They became the first K-pop girl group to perform at Coachella in 2019. Their name reflects the idea that things that seem pretty can also have a dark, powerful side.

questions.question: Which music industry event gathers over 250 songwriters, producers, and artists for 200 recording sessions across 40 studios in just 5 days?
questions.explanation: Anti Social Camp is an intensive, large-scale songwriting camp that packs an extraordinary volume of creative collaboration into a single week. With 200 sessions spread across 40 studios, it's designed to foster rapid, high-output music creation among hundreds of industry professionals. The event's name playfully contrasts with its highly social, collaborative nature.

questions.question: Which pioneering peer-to-peer music sharing service shut down its servers on July 11, 2001, following a legal battle with the Recording Industry Association of America?
questions.explanation: Napster, founded by Shawn Fanning and Sean Parker in 1999, was forced to shut down its servers on July 11, 2001, after losing a landmark copyright infringement lawsuit brought by the RIAA and several major record labels. At its peak, Napster had over 80 million registered users and fundamentally disrupted the music industry. The service briefly attempted a paid relaunch before ultimately being sold and rebranded multiple times.
